Round 1 preserved at eval/judge-scores-r1.json (versioning-by-suffix, aif-c01 precedent). Scope of the rework under judgment: commit 168ae1f restated item 1.10's stem as constraints and re-glossed keyed option C with an off-stem mechanism detail; options A, B, D unchanged; rationale rewritten. METHOD: all 68 items re-read in full and every distractor argued FOR before scoring, INDEPENDENTLY of round 1 - the round-2 grid was formed first (including an independent re-measurement of stem/option content-word overlap across the whole bank) and only then compared with round 1. Outcome of that comparison: 373 of 408 dimension scores identical; 32 single-point differences across 26 items reconciled to round 1's published calibration statement (each recorded in that item's `case`; three of them touched the 3/4 boundary - 1.07 dim 2, 2.04 dim 2 and dim 5 - and none changed Gate 2 sample membership); 3 differences HELD as round-2 deltas (1.10 dim 2 and dim 5, the verified rework; 4.08 dim 4, a round-1 miss). The `case` field this round records the delta or reconciliation judgment; the full round-1 distractor cases remain in the r1 file and were re-checked against the current option text. RESULT: zero dimensions <=2 anywhere - NO BOUNCES in round 2. Dimension-5 distribution moved from 20x5 / 39x4 / 8x3 / 1x2 (round 1) to 20x5 / 40x4 / 8x3 / 0x2. Gate 2 auto-flags from 3s: 10 items.

REWORKED ITEM - scored fresh under §bounce (full rubric, new blind solve, no partial credit). Argued FOR each distractor against the new stem: B (one-time bulk export restored during a scheduled overnight outage) is the strongest and is now a real competitor - it is the ordinary way a data tier is moved, and it is defeated only by reading the two constraints together (a window of minutes, and no write lost); D (rebuild in a different engine as part of the move) is a genuine migration strategy that a team carrying an old schema really does propose, and loses as unrequested re-architecture; A (defer the move, accept a stale copy) is a real portfolio-sequencing answer and loses because every stated constraint keeps applying while it waits. ROUND-1 DEFECT VERIFIED FIXED: the stem now states constraints only (round-the-clock writes, minutes-long cutover, no write lost) and no longer states the mechanism, and keyed option C carries an off-stem mechanism detail (ongoing change capture applied to the target). Re-measured stem/key content-word overlap: key = 1 shared word, the LOWEST of the four options (max distractor 3, option D) - inverted from round 1's 9-vs-4 key-high margin, so the string-match route is gone and the item now requires the constraint-to-strategy mapping that concept C-010 names. Dim 5 2 -> 4 (a near-neighbour resolved on recall, not a surface giveaway; not 5 because 'no write may be lost' is a fairly direct signpost once the option set is known). Dim 2 3 -> 4 (B and D compete properly now that the stem no longer pre-commits; A is the weaker of the three). Rationale rewritten with the key named and distractor A re-argued on its own terms - dim 4 holds at 5. BOUNCE CLEARED.

Re-argued FOR each distractor: A (AWS Prescriptive Guidance) is the strongest - it is real published material and a volunteer administrator would plausibly look there first; it loses because the question has already outrun what was written in advance. D (buy a plan for one question) is a real instinct defeated by the stem's no-urgency, no-budget framing. B (Trust and Safety) is off-axis and eliminable without engaging, which caps dim 2 at 4. ROUND-2 DELTA, HELD AGAINST ROUND 1: dim 4 lowered 5 -> 4. rationale.correct argues the principle as 'what the community question-and-answer service is for' and never names AWS re:Post, so a candidate revising from the rationale alone cannot carry the service name back to their study material. This is the same house-style gap round 1 recorded on nine items (2.06, 2.19, 3.14, 3.17, 3.19, 3.20, 3.21, 3.22, 3.23); 4.08 was missed there. Evidence for ratchet proposal 2 is therefore 10 items, not 9. Not a bounce - a 4 ships.

bounce_resolution.1.10: RESOLVED (commit 168ae1f), verified on this tree. Round-1 record: defect_class answer-surface-cue (stem-restatement variant), dim 5 = 2, dim 2 = 3 noted; required fix was two edits - restate the stem as constraint rather than mechanism, and re-gloss keyed option C with an off-stem mechanism detail, keeping A, B and D. Both edits landed and nothing else in the item changed. Independent re-measurement on this tree: stem/keyed-option content-word overlap is now 1 (was 9), the lowest of the four options, against a maximum of 3 for any distractor (was 4) - the key-high margin that defined the defect is inverted. Fresh round-2 blind solve of the reworked item: answered C at high confidence, reasoning recorded pre-key as 'minutes of cutover with zero lost writes requires ongoing replication/change capture, not a bulk export' - i.e. solved from the constraints, which is the concept the item is built on. Full re-score 5/4/5/5/4/5, no dimension <=2, bounce cleared. 1.10 is carried into the Gate 2 sample as a bounce survivor so a human confirms the fix. Ratchet: the stem-key-word-match validator check proposed by round 1 (eval-report round 1 §8.1) remains unimplemented and outside this session's ownership; until it lands, this defect class is caught only by examiner measurement.
